name: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (silicon, BC108C, c. 1969-70)
description: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face, NPN silicon version (BC108C; BC109C, BC183L, BC209C were also fitted), negative ground, +9 V battery. Two direct-coupled common-emitter stages with shunt-series feedback: C1 2.2 µF into the Q1 base (no pull-down, no input buffer: the guitar sees the 5-8 kΩ input impedance of the stage), Q1 emitter grounded, 33 kΩ Q1 collector load, Q1 collector driving the Q2 base; Q2 collector through 8.2 kΩ to a node that goes to +9 V through 330 Ω (the germanium version's 470 Ω) and out through 0.01 µF to the 500 kΩ audio Volume pot; Q2 emitter to ground through the 1 kΩ linear Fuzz pot, whose wiper is bypassed by 20 µF; 100 kΩ from the Q2 emitter back to the Q1 base. Effect-on (DPDT true-bypass) state.

sources.title: Fuzz Central, 'Arbiter Fuzz Face' (original NPN silicon schematic 'fuzzfacenpnschematic.gif': 2.2 µF, 33K, 8K2, 330 Ω, 100K, 0.01 µF, Volume 500KA, Fuzz 1KB, 20 µF; transistors BC108C, BC109, BC109C, BC183L, BC209C; 'the 470-ohm resistor was replaced with a 330-ohm'; negative ground +9 V)
Experimentalists Anonymous, Fuzz Face schematic PDF (NPN silicon BC108C version: the 470 Ω becomes 330 Ω, battery and electrolytics reversed)
ElectroSmash, 'Fuzz Face Analysis' (topology, shunt-series feedback, input impedance 5.2-8.4 kΩ, bias targets, output divider). Archived copy used
BC107/BC108/BC109 datasheet (Philips/NXP, hFE group C 420-800) for the BC108C stand-in model

lte.note: LTE substeps start on BDF2 and continue in trapezoid (docs §10.61): a backward-Euler restart on every continued sample was this unit's largest integration error. Engine 8x fine-step truth, audio band, lead / rock DI: 0.023 / 0.064 % -> 0.0055 / 0.014 %; ngspice ffsi_lead_d32 out 0.026 -> 0.012 %. CPU equal (9900X)

multirate.note: Event-local oversampling (docs §10.48, §10.62): the circuit runs at 768 kHz and every LTE event takes 4 substeps (3.07 MHz) into the band-limited output stream. The near-square edges carry content up to MHz: at a fixed 768 kHz they fold (aliasing gate, every bin, 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 FS: -57.6 / -55.9 / -50.1 dB), and even a fixed 1.536 MHz or 2-substep events leave -57.5 to -61.5 dB at 1.0 FS. Now -83.1 / -76.0 / -69.6 dB. Engine 8x fine-step truth (band-limited), audio band, lead / rock DI: 0.030 / 0.026 -> 0.030 / 0.009 %

BC108C.note: unverified: no vendor SPICE card found. BF 520 is inside the BC108C hFE group C range (420-800); IS 20 fA and BR 5 are assumed small-signal silicon values. Real units vary widely; builders often pick lower gain CJE 9p / CJC 4.5p from the BC108 datasheet typical Cib / Cob (assumed for the C grade).

controls.label: Volume
controls.note: 500 kΩ audio-taper pot after the 0.01 µF output cap; wiper is the output

controls.label: Fuzz
controls.note: 1 kΩ linear pot from the Q2 emitter (pin 3) to ground (pin 1), wiper bypassed by 20 µF: clockwise bypasses more of the emitter resistance (more gain, less feedback)

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: Legacy 'Bass' parameter. The Fuzz Face has only Volume and Fuzz; no circuit meaning, stored only

controls.label: Treble
controls.note: Legacy 'Treble' parameter; no such knob; no circuit meaning, stored only

controls.label: Lamp
controls.note: Legacy indicator lamp. The original has no LED; stored only

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; the circuit is mono, stored only

parts.label: 9 V battery (negative ground)
parts.note: Ideal source. ElectroSmash notes the battery's internal resistance adds to the 330/470 Ω and changes the output level; a fresh PP3 is about 1-2 Ω (not modelled)

parts.label: Collector top resistor (330 Ω in the silicon version)
